description: Triggers when a new message is received in Gmail.
instructions:
**Instructions for Setting Up the Trigger:**

    - Ensure that the Gmail API is enabled for your Google account.
    - Provide the user ID (usually 'me' for the authenticated user).
    - Optionally, provide label IDs to filter messages.
    
    **Using the Trigger as a Webhook (Gmail Push Notifications)**

    By default the trigger polls Gmail on its interval and needs no setup. To
    use it as a webhook trigger, so Gmail notifies Composio as soon as the
    mailbox changes, set up push notifications on your own Google OAuth app,
    the one your Gmail auth config uses. Do this once per OAuth app. With the
    Composio Gmail app, the trigger keeps polling.

    1. In the Google Cloud project that owns the OAuth client, enable the
       Gmail API and the Cloud Pub/Sub API.
    2. Create a Pub/Sub topic in that project. Its full name is
       `projects/<project-id>/topics/<topic-id>`.
    3. On the topic, grant `gmail-api-push@system.gserviceaccount.com` the
       Pub/Sub Publisher role (`roles/pubsub.publisher`).
    4. Create a service account in that project only for push deliveries,
       for example `composio-gmail-push`. Give it no roles and create no
       keys for it: Pub/Sub uses it only to sign each push.
    5. Register a webhook endpoint for Gmail with the OAuth client ID. On it,
       set `topic_name` (Pub/Sub Topic Name) to the topic's full name,
       `push_service_account_email` (Push Service Account) to the service
       account's email, and `push_audience` (Push Audience) to the
       `webhook_url` the endpoint returns.
    6. Create a push subscription on the topic. Set its endpoint URL to that
       `webhook_url`. Turn on authentication, choose the service account,
       and set the audience to the same `webhook_url`. Leave payload
       unwrapping off, and set the expiration period to never expire.
       Composio rejects any push whose Google-signed token names another
       service account or audience.

    Whoever creates the subscription needs the Service Account User role on
    the service account; project Owners and Editors already have it. If
    pushes don't arrive, check that Pub/Sub's service agent,
    `service-<project-number>@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, can
    sign tokens for the account, and if not, grant it the Service Account
    Token Creator role on the account.

    Google documents its side of this setup in
    https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/push and
    https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/authenticate-push-subscriptions.
name: New Gmail Message Received Trigger

description:
Triggers when a new Notion database (the container) is created.

A database is the post-2025-09-03 container that holds one or more data
sources. This trigger fires for the container's creation event
(`database.created`), distinct from `NOTION_DATASOURCE_CREATED` which
fires when a new data source is added to an existing database.

or creating a database via the Notion UI will see this event. Adding a
new data source to an existing database fires `data_source.created`
instead — use `NOTION_DATASOURCE_CREATED` for that.

Notion's payload puts `entity.type: "block"` (the container is a
`child_database` block in the content tree) and `entity.id` is the
database id.

        2. Enable events.
        3. Input the 'Request URL' field with `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/trigger_instances/slack/default/handle`

      app to the channels you want to monitor. In case using Composio Slack app,

**Instructions for Setting Up the Trigger:**

    - If you are using your own Slack app:
        1. Go to the 'Event Subscriptions' section of your app's settings.
        2. Enable events.
        3. Input the 'Request URL' field with `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/trigger_instances/slack/default/handle`
        4. Add `channel_created` to the 'Subscribe to bot events' section and
          `Subscribe to events on behalf of users` section and save.
    - If you are using the Composio Slack app, you are all set here!
    - If you are using Slackbot integration, you would need to add the Slack
      app to the channels you want to monitor. In case using Composio Slack app,
      you need to do /add and then choose Composio App.
